items.title: Respect `target` on <a/> tags under Link
items.body:
There are occasions where it is useful to have `target='_blank'` on hyperlinks within your own app. (For example, if your app is being loaded in an iframe and you'd like for the links to break out in to new windows.)

With this PR, the `onClick` logic in Link now checks for an external target on the nested <a/> tag, and will fall back to the default behavior if it's present, similar to the logic for shift-/cmd-clicking the link.

items.title: improve custom-server-fastify example
items.body:
I’ve been experimenting with Next.js and Fastify and I made the following changes to the Fastify example based on what I found:

### Use Fastify’s plugin API
IMO putting Fastify’s listen call in a promise callback is an anti-pattern, b/c the Fastify plugin API is meant to solve the problem of async server bootstrapping.

[From Fastify’s Getting Started docs](https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Getting-Started/):
> Fastify provides a foundation that assists with the asynchronous bootstrapping of your application.

### Set reply.sent in handlers which return promises

[From Fastify’s Routes docs](https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Routes/#promise-resolution):
> If your handler is an `async` function or returns a promise, you should be aware of a special behaviour which is necessary to support the callback and promise control-flow. If the handler's promise is resolved with `undefined`, it will be ignored causing the request to hang and an *error* log to be emitted.
>
> 1. If you want to use `async/await` or promises but respond a value with `reply.send`:
>     - **Don't** `return` any value.
>     - **Don't** forget to call `reply.send`.
> 2. If you want to use `async/await` or promises:
>     - **Don't** use `reply.send`.
>     - **Don't** return `undefined`.

`app.render` returns a promise which contains undefined, so returning it in a Fastify handler will log an error. However, returning anything besides undefined will cause Fastify to try to write to the response which Next.js has already ended. The solution is to manually set the `reply.sent` flag to true when any Next.js rendering promise is fulfilled as an alternative to calling `reply.send`.

### Make Next.js handle 404 errors
This allows any route to throw a NotFound error and let Next.js handle the rendering of the 404 page.

### Make Next.js handle any route which starts with `_next` in dev
This prevents dev routes from being caught by user-defined routes.

items.title: Compile pages to .next/static directory
items.body:
The way Next.js has always worked was by resolving:

```
// url path
_next/{buildid}/page/index.js
```

To 

```
// server path
.next/bundles/pages/index.js
```

As you can see there's a difference between the URL path and the path on the filesystem. 

This created some downsides:

- The files have to be served by custom logic in the Next.js server, so these files couldn't be served directly by another web server, e.g. nginx to improve the performance of serving files without having it hit the origin Node.js server. Note that this downside isn't the case when using https://now.sh with [the Now CDN](https://zeit.co/cdn) 
- Next export has to copy the directory separately
- 2 routes were responsible for serving page bundles. (1 for .js and 1 for .js.map)
- on demand entries logic was colocated with these 2 routes.

What this PR aims to do is remove the 2 routes + extra next export logic and serve the pages directly from `.next/static`.

The new path to pages is:

```
// url path
_next/static/{buildid}/pages/index.js
```

To 

```
// server path
.next/static/{buildid}/pages/index.js
```

This also partially solves another issue for when users run `next build` on the same server where production is running, as it won't override the existing files.

items.title: Fix missing polyfills
items.body:
## Issue

Since IE11 doesn't support Promises and Next.js needs them for [dynamic imports](https://webpack.js.org/guides/code-splitting/#dynamic-imports) we need to add a polyfill for them.

Before the upgrade to Babel 7 Next.js was using [babel-plugin-transform-runtime](https://www.npmjs.com/package/babel-plugin-transform-runtime), a package that automatically added polyfills by referencing them from core-js.

This has been changed in Babel v7: https://babeljs.io/docs/en/next/v7-migration#babel-runtime-babel-plugin-transform-runtime. From now on core-js isn't included per default. I think this is a good thing! 

## Solution

~~There are many different ways I could have fixed this issue. One way could have been to re-add core-js to Next.js. This probably would have been the safest way. But this would also add polyfills to the node.js based files (plus polyfills for e.g. `Set`, `Map`, …).~~

~~Thats why I chose an explicit polyfill. Just for the client part of the Next.js.~~

Edit: Using an explicit polyfill breaks a lot in IE11. Since we also need to polyfill object assign & more.

## Alternatives

- Use core-js@2 + babel-plugin-transform-runtime
- Use Webpack provide plugin
- Deprecate IE11 & Change the documentation 

## Related

Closes: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/4988
Related: https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/5006

--------------

Please note that I am not an expert on this topic. Please carefully question my thoughts.

items.title: withApollo example - move from old HOC APIs to new function-as-child APIs
Introduce dynamic(() => import())
items.body:
Fixes #5221
Fixes #5208
Fixes #5213

Bringing back some old non-standard behavior:

```js
import dynamic from 'next/dynamic'

const HelloWorld = dynamic(import('../components/hello-world'))

export default () => <HelloWorld />
```

Will compile to:

```js
import dynamic from 'next/dynamic'

const HelloWorld = dynamic(() => import('../components/hello-world'))

export default () => <HelloWorld />
```

- `next/dynamic` accepts a loader function as first argument
- `next/dynamic` usage with just `dynamic(import())` is transpiled to a loader function, 

The reason for these changes is that calling `import()` will immediately load the module when the code is executed, which is what most users don't want. This is to mirror Next 6 and below behavior around this syntax. Do note that it's non-standard and has to be deprecated. We can easily write a codemod to change this usage to the new loader function syntax.

- We now send the webpack moduleIds to the client side so that the `preloadReady` react-loadable function can filter out only the modules needed for hydration, instead of loading everything and waiting for that. This will introduce a performance boost when you *are* using `next/dynamic` but also make sure that modules aren't loaded when you don't render them.

### TODO v7.1

- Make the transpiled function log a warning with an err.sh link that explains how to run the codemod
- Write codemod

items.title: Speed up build && remove ignore plugin
items.body:
During the review of the build flow I have noticed that ignorePlugin from webpack take a lot of time:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3331480/46598989-abe8fb80-caee-11e8-9301-9cc2c6093535.png)

And I think there are no needs for this two ignore plugins calls, so I propose to remove them in case to speed up build time:

1)`/(precomputed)/, /node_modules.+(elliptic)/` - It was added almost 1 year ago and I think it was added to prevent adding elliptic module to prod build. This `elliptic` is going from webpack so there are no ways when it will be added to build files. https://github.com/zeit/next.js/blame/202ceca1af1baeab5f61d2812ec48b019c80919d/server/build/webpack.js#L108

2)`/prop-types-exact/.test(resource)` - there is only one component where in next.js used `prop-types-exact` - in Link component. But it adds `prop-types-exact` only in dev mode. So as a result `prop-types-exact` skipped in prod version and it just waste time during the build trying to find this module. That's why I propose to remove it and allow to add it manually who is really needed it, because not all projects add this module.

After removing these rows, there is no increase of bundle size or something like this. Only speed up of build time. Here is a difference based on my project.
1) Before:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3331480/46599422-06368c00-caf0-11e8-9e49-b10f99f554c1.png)
2)After: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3331480/46599484-25cdb480-caf0-11e8-835b-d78c2411161c.png)

items.title: Add Typescript types for builds functions
Fix paths when built on windows
items.body:
This PR Fixes #4920

So the problem is that when a next.js application is built on windows, the `pages-manifest.json` file is created with backslashes. If this built application is deployed to a linux hosting enviroment, the server will fail when trying to load the modules.

```
Error: Cannot find module '/user_code/next/server/bundles\pages\index.js
```

My simple solution is to modify the `pages-manifest.json` to always use linux separator (`/`), then also 
modify `server/require.js` to, when requiring page, replace any separator (`\` or `/`) with current platform-specific file separator (`require('path').sep`).

The fix in `server/require.js` would be sufficient, but my opinion is that having some cross-platform consistency is nice.

This change was tested by bulding an application in windows and running it in linux and windows, aswell as building an application in linux and running it in linux and windows. The related tests was also run.

items.title: multi-threaded export with nice progress indication
items.body:
This PR will

- allow nextjs export to use all available CPU cores for rendering & writing pages by using child_process
- make use of async-sema to allow each thread to concurrently write multiple paths

items.title: Fix #5674 Append crossOrigin on the client side too, add config option for crossOrigin
items.body:
# Fixes https://github.com/zeit/next.js/issues/5674

This adds config option
```js
// next.config.js
module.exports = {
  crossOrigin: 'anonymous'
}
```
This config option is defined in the webpack Define Plugin at build.
`Head` and `NextScript` now use the config option, if it's not explicitly set on the element.
This value is now passed to Webpack so it can add it to scripts that it loads.
The value is now used in `PageLoader` (on the client) so it can add it to the scripts and links that it loads.
Using `<Head crossOrigin>` or `<NextScript crossOrigin>` is now deprecated.
